Read a Praat TextGrid in any text encoding

Source: R/landmarks.R
read_textgrid.Rd

Reads a TextGrid saved as a Praat text file (long or short format) and parses it with rPraat::tg.read(). Praat saves a TextGrid as UTF-16 whenever a label or tier name is not plain ASCII (Chinese characters or IPA, for example), and rPraat::tg.read() cannot read those files on its own. Here the file is converted to UTF-8 first, so UTF-16 (with or without a byte-order mark), UTF-8 and older 8-bit encodings all read the same way.

Usage

read_textgrid(path, name = basename(path))

Arguments

path

Path to a .TextGrid file.

name

File name to use in the note. Defaults to the file's own name; give the original name when path is a temporary copy, as with a Shiny upload.

Value

A list with five elements:

  • tg: the TextGrid as returned by rPraat::tg.read() (a named list of tiers), or NULL when the file could not be read.

  • encoding: the encoding the file was read as, such as "UTF-16BE", "UTF-8" or a guessed code page ("CP1252", "GB18030", "BIG5"); NA when the file could not be decoded.

  • reason: NULL on success; otherwise a short phrase saying why the file could not be read, such as "it is in Praat's binary format; in Praat, use Save as text file".

  • note: NULL, or a sentence for the user when the code page was guessed or bytes that are not UTF-8 were replaced.

  • stray_lines: NULL, or the numbers of the lines that held bytes that are not UTF-8 in a file otherwise read as UTF-8.

Details

A file with no byte-order mark that is not valid UTF-8 was saved in an 8-bit code page, which has to be guessed, as for read_csv_utf8(). Praat's own 8-bit files (its "try ISO Latin-1" preference) read as Windows-1252, and files with mostly Chinese text as GBK or Big5. The result then has a note that says so. A UTF-8 file with a few bytes that are not UTF-8 stays UTF-8 instead, as in read_csv_utf8(): those bytes are shown as U+FFFD (the replacement character), and note and stray_lines say where.

Praat writes a double quote inside a label or tier name as two (""); these are turned back into one, as Praat shows them. Labels are otherwise kept exactly as written: no Unicode normalisation is applied.

Praat's binary and chronological TextGrid formats cannot be read. Open such a file in Praat and use Save as text file.

Examples

# A short-format TextGrid with a Chinese label, saved as UTF-16BE with a
# byte-order mark, as Praat does by default
txt <- paste('File type = "ooTextFile"', 'Object class = "TextGrid"', "",
             "0", "0.5", "<exists>", "1", '"IntervalTier"', '"syllable"',
             "0", "0.5", "1", "0", "0.5",
             paste0('"', intToUtf8(0x5988), '"'), sep = "\n")
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".TextGrid")
writeBin(c(as.raw(c(0xFE, 0xFF)),
           iconv(txt, "UTF-8", "UTF-16BE", toRaw = TRUE)[[1]]), f)
if (requireNamespace("rPraat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  r <- read_textgrid(f)
  r$encoding
  r$tg$syllable$label
}
#> [1] "妈"
